title: Compile open ride-acceleration datasets with provenance
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. Design load cases (docs/research/ride-acceleration-data.md) rest on a few published figures. Openly licensed measured traces (papers' supplementary data, physics-education datasets, open smartphone recordings) would let the arrest model use real pulses.
objective: Collect openly licensed, measured ride acceleration time series, normalise them to a common CSV schema (time s, ax, ay, az in g, ride-frame axes documented) and write a datasheet for each.
acceptanceCriteria: Only data whose licence allows redistribution is included; licence and source recorded per file
CSV schema documented; each file has a datasheet (ride type, sensor, sample rate, mounting, axes, known issues)
A summary table of peak -Gz per dataset with pulse duration
No data copied from paid standards
Data CC-BY-4.0 (or the source's compatible licence), any scripts MIT
